citation.source: Commonly cited culinary conversion: 1 pinch ≈ 1/16 tsp of fine table salt
citation.note: Same figure as salted-fried-potatoes.json — genuinely imprecise by convention, not just uncited.

metadata.notes: The concrete, runnable proof of 'how frying potatoes actually works' in this vocabulary, added 2026-08-13 — every existing recipe (salted-fried-potatoes.json, garlic-oil-potatoes.json, tortilla-de-patatas.json) uses FRY as a single generic step with no oilTempC/doneness and a chunky 'diced' shape; none of them exercise the double-fry pipeline or the shape/temperature reasoning that's actually built. This recipe deliberately ties all three pieces together on one dish: shape='julienne' (CUT, a real state, ~matchstick-thin — the shape Thermoworks' cited method assumes for its stated ratios), PAR_FRY at 163°C/270s (the cited par-fry stage: starch gelatinizes, interior cooks through, stays pale), then FRY at 191°C/180s with doneness='golden' (the cited finishing stage: steam-driven crisping of the exterior). See data/actions/par-fry.json and data/actions/fry.json for the full citations (Kalogianni & Smith 2013, IJFST; Thermoworks) — not re-derived here.
metadata.restGapNote: This sequence goes directly from PAR_FRY to FRY with no step in between, even though the same cited source (par-fry.json's restNote) specifies a real ~10-minute rest between the two stages. Not silently glossed over: this repo has no REST verb (ROADMAP.md's 'More common technique verbs' still lists it as open), so there is currently no way to express that interval in a RecipeScript at all — this recipe is the concrete case that gap actually blocks, not a hypothetical one.
metadata.shapeConnectionNote: The 'julienne' shape here is chosen because it matches the cited source's assumption, not because this schema computed it or requires it — potato.json's fryingScienceNote already names this precisely: nothing connects CUT's shape state to PAR_FRY's/FRY's own durationSeconds. Partially closed 2026-08-15: src/recipe-explain.ts's fry-timing-vs-geometry check (cut-dimensions.ts + heat-penetration.ts) now flags exactly this class of mismatch as a pre-flight ADVISORY — running this recipe through npm run validate-recipe reports zero timing advisories, a real, computed confirmation that julienne (1.6-3.2mm) at 163C/270s then 191C/180s comfortably clears the real time needed for the center to reach a fork-tender temperature (checked directly, not just asserted). Still NOT enforced by engine.ts/applyAction itself — same informational-only distinction every other advisory in this repo draws — a recipe author picking a thicker shape with the same durations would still execute successfully via runRecipe, just with a pre-flight warning attached, not a rejection.
